promotion_note: Promoted 2026-07-29 (owner instruction, pjm-137 session). EXACTLY ONE config delta vs the superseded 2026-07-28-pjm-136-lossurf: measured_ct_heat_rates False -> True. The pjm-136 recipe is otherwise carried VERBATIM (its own pjm_zonal_loss_surface delta, pjm-135's net-position cut and pjm-133's hydro budget all preserved), and the A/B control arm pjm137_control_A reproduces the superseded keeper BYTE-IDENTICALLY -- 0.000000000 MW over 166,440 class-hours in each of 2023/2024/2025 -- so the delta is provably isolated. MECHANISM (zero DOF): each CT_PEAKER plant's heat_rate becomes its MEASURED LOADED rate in place of the eGRID plant-average ANNUAL rate, from the existing frozen derive (rule 23) run for PJM for the first time (scripts/data/derive_campd_ct_heat_rates.py --iso PJM -> campd_ct_heat_rates_PJM.csv, 71 plants, ALL inside the physical simple-cycle band [6.0, 25.0] MMBtu/MWh net, ZERO excluded). Per unit the rate is sum(heatInput)/sum(grossLoad) over hours >= 0.8 x that unit's own p95 gross load (>= 50 qualifying hours), converted to a NET basis by the committed parasitic factor -- the SAME map the benchmark's net actual uses -- and generation-weighted across the plant's turbines. No scale, no haircut, no blend, no per-plant override. The DOF ledger goes 16 -> 17 entries with n_residual UNCHANGED at 6. Rule 19: this owns the CT_PEAKER loaded heat rate ONLY; CT_CHP is outside the derive's scope and nothing else in the offer path moves. Rule 25: PJM's artifact from PJM's own plants -- NYISO's keeper verdict (nyiso-89) does NOT cross the boundary. DRIVER (rule 14 [R-ACCURATE], not a residual): the eGRID figure is an ESTIMATE and it is demonstrably wrong at a mixed facility, because eGRID publishes ONE heat rate per PLANT. Doswell Energy Center is the case in point: the model fleet splits it into 6 CC_REGULAR + 3 CT_PEAKER generators ALL carrying the single plant average of 9.027 MMBtu/MWh, while its simple-cycle turbines MEASURE 11.350 -- the model was undercharging those peakers by 2.32 MMBtu/MWh, about $8/MWh. Across PJM the correction is a MEASUREMENT, not a multiplier: 29 of 71 plants move by more than 0.5 MMBtu/MWh, 35 cheaper and 36 dearer, ISO energy-weighted +0.229 MMBtu/MWh (~ +$0.80/MWh at $3.50/MMBtu). CHARTERED BY FINDING-pjm137-dominion-congestion-is-subzonal-2026-07-29.md, which CLOSED the question pjm-136 section 5 handed forward ('make an internal PJM constraint actually price, or prove it can't') with the second branch. PJM's own day-ahead binding-constraint record (new intake data/raw/pjm-binding-constraints/, DataMiner2 da_marginal_value, 228,795 constraint-hours) puts only 6.34/3.06/6.19 % of its congestion rent on a named zonal-scale interface and 80.0-87.8 % on monitored facilities rated 230 kV and below; AEP-DOM -- the very boundary the pjm-133..136 lineage tried to make price -- carries 0.041/0.071/0.236 %. In the top-decile DOM-separation hours the dominant constraints are PLEASNTV TX3 500 kV, GOOSECRE TX1 500 kV, PLEASNTV-ASHBURN 230 kV, ASHBURN-GOOSECRE 230 kV and BRAMBLET-EVRGREEN, every one of which returns zone = DOM from PJM's own pnode registry -- BOTH ends inside PJM_Dominion. And PJM's 500 kV EHV nodes (new intake data/raw/pjm-ehv-lmp/) measure MORE price dispersion INSIDE the Dominion zone ($6.18/$8.68/$16.78) than across the whole DOM-AEP boundary ($4.76/$6.13/$14.42), a ratio of 1.30/1.42/1.16x. That is the ERCOT/MISO internal_congestion_split refusal class, now established for PJM on PJM's own numbers. GATES (PREREG-pjm137-measured-ct-heat-rates-2026-07-29.md, committed and pushed BEFORE either arm solved, including its own section 2a correction): determination CALIBRATED with EVERY criterion passing, C1 16/16 with free 12/12 in BOTH arms, C2/C3a/C3b/C3c/C4/C6/C7/C8 all PASS. K1 the C3c standing kill -- C3c PASSES and is UNCHANGED, the model's tail-hour counts identical at 3/10/32 h, so the keeper's thinnest margin was not touched. P2 material and two-signed (29/71 beyond 0.5 MMBtu/MWh, 35 cheaper / 36 dearer). K3 zero plants excluded by the physical band (0.00 % of energy). K4 ZERO slack and ZERO dump in both arms, all years. K5 the control arm byte-identical. K6 no new rows or columns -- coefficient values only. ZONAL RESULT: Dominion CT_PEAKER 0.724 -> 0.721 / 1.380 -> 1.448 / 2.923 -> 3.162 TWh while the ISO-WIDE CT_PEAKER class FALLS 2.857/2.635/2.794 TWh -- pure reallocation toward the deficit zone, the same signature pjm-136 produced and for a different reason (a per-PLANT re-pricing moves energy from the zones whose peakers the eGRID average most over-credited). Against the benchmark's own actual the Dominion gap goes -2.342 -> -2.345 / -2.668 -> -2.600 / -2.295 -> -2.056, closing 10.4 % of the 2025 gap. THE PRE-REGISTRATION WAS REFUTED ON ITS OWN EXPECTED DIRECTION and is recorded as such rather than re-written: PREREG section 4 predicted the delta would push the Dominion leg the WRONG way because Dominion's energy-weighted rate rises the most of any zone (+0.634 MMBtu/MWh). It did rise, and Dominion still gained, because the mechanism is PER PLANT -- Doswell (+2.324) and Gravel Neck (+3.204) are correctly made dearer while Remington (-0.329) and Ladysmith (-0.001) are not. HONEST SCOPE, carried and never dropped: (a) ISO-wide CT_PEAKER volume moves FURTHER from its EIA-923 class total in two of three years (|error| 0.75 -> 2.11 in 2023 and 0.94 -> 3.57 in 2024) while 2025 improves markedly (6.11 -> 3.32); C1 still passes 16/16 so no band breaks, but the class-level trade is real -- CC_REGULAR (7.42 -> 6.07, 3.03 -> 1.84) and COAL_BIT (0.87 -> 0.29, 2.15 -> 1.62) both improve as CT energy moves into them. (b) C8 CT_PEAKER forced share RISES to 16.3/16.9/17.1 % (2023 newly above the 15 % peaker cap); all three are GROUNDED -- every binding mechanism clears D-4, profile r 0.923-0.973 and off-peak CV ratio 0.703-1.083 -- so under rule 20 this is a clean PASS surfaced as a report note, but it is a shrinking class carrying a larger forced fraction and the next session should watch it. (c) The delta does not address the CONGESTION half of the Dominion price deficit and never claimed to. (d) C3c still passes by only ~1 h (2024) and ~2.5 h (2025) against a 0.5x floor -- inherited from pjm-136, unchanged here, still the thinnest margin in the keeper. (e) Dominion CC_REGULAR 2025 still OVERSHOOTS the actual, inherited from pjm-136. Rule 1 [R-STRUCT] / rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] order of reasoning, for the record: the delta was chartered because the measured loaded rate is more accurate than the estimate it replaces -- demonstrably so at a mixed facility -- and the pre-registration recorded, before any arm solved, that it was expected to move the chartered defect the WRONG way and would be kept anyway. The rubric movement is a consequence, not the justification. PREREG section 4's no-feedback ceiling was honoured: no multiplier, blend, scale, floor, cap, per-plant override or band widening was applied to the derived rates, and none may be. Full write-up: results/calibration/FINDING-pjm137-dominion-congestion-is-subzonal-2026-07-29.md. Supersedes 2026-07-28-pjm-136-lossurf.
note: Open ROOT CAUSES. (1) THE ZONAL-CONGESTION ROUTE TO THE DOMINION CT LEG IS CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT (pjm-137). PJM's own binding-constraint record puts 3.1-6.3 % of its DA congestion rent on zonal-scale interfaces and 0.04-0.24 % on AEP-DOM; the constraints that dominate the DOM-separation hours are Loudoun-County 500/230 kV facilities with BOTH ends inside PJM_Dominion; and intra-Dominion EHV dispersion ($6.18/$8.68/$16.78) EXCEEDS the inter-zonal DOM-AEP spread ($4.76/$6.13/$14.42). Do NOT propose another zonal congestion mechanism for this defect. (2) THE DEFECT HAS BEEN OVERSTATED ~1.9x IN THIS NOTE'S OWN PREDECESSORS: the Dominion CT_PEAKER actual is 3.066/4.048/5.218 TWh on the benchmark's own unit-split per-plant record, NOT the 7.38/8.68/9.64 every prior handoff carried -- that figure is the nine roster plants' WHOLE-PLANT energy and counts Doswell's combined-cycle blocks (4.45 TWh in 2025) as peaker output. The real gap after pjm-137 is -2.345/-2.600/-2.056 TWh, i.e. the model is at 24/36/61 % of actual. Always take a zonal class actual from frontend/data/backcast/bench/<ISO>/<year>.json.gz, which carries split: 'unit_hourly' at mixed sites. (3) THE SUCCESSOR'S TARGET, RESTATED ON THE CORRECTED HOUR KEY (pjm-138 A1 + pjm-139). The Dominion CT-hour price deficit is $17.97/$26.44/$54.06 per MWh, NOT the $17.72/$26.69/$54.61 this note carried: pjm-137's measured-side loader indexed Eastern PREVAILING time against a model and a CAMPD record that are BOTH Eastern STANDARD, so from March to November its series sat one hour ahead of both. Levels move only $0.12-0.38/MWh and every pjm-137 conclusion stands (the correlation improves 0.704->0.745, 0.732->0.764, 0.772->0.823), but NO diurnal statistic may be quoted from _pjm137_dominion_ct_congestion.py -- use _pjm138_mec_gap_shape.py's UTC-keyed loader. OF THAT DEFICIT, ONLY 8.1/23.1/22.1 % IS REACHABLE: pjm-137 closed 54.6/51.8/54.2 % as intra-zonal congestion and pjm-138 attributes 37.3/25.2/26.2 % to the reserve opportunity cost the no-MIP LP structurally cannot price, leaving $1.46/$6.12/$11.97 per MWh for ANY energy-stack mechanism. Crediting the measured reserve price takes the ANNUAL load-weighted system-energy gap to -$2.36/-$0.08/+$2.76 -- the energy stack's LEVEL is right and the residual is SHAPE ONLY, so any lever must raise tight hours WITHOUT raising slack ones. AND THE REACHABLE SHARE IS CONCENTRATED, NOT SPREAD ACROSS CT HOURS (pjm-139): it lives in the WINTER MORNING RAMP. DJF h06-h07 CT-weighted the residual after both closed lanes is $3.93/$30.48/$40.11 (load-weighted after the reserve credit -$0.37/+$5.55/+$13.44, so 2023 is fully explained and 2024-25 are not), while DJF midday and overnight run NEGATIVE -- the model is too DEAR there. The defect is a RAMP-RATE deficit, not a level or a fuel-price one: PJM's own DJF system energy price rises +$15.28/+$21.63/+$35.45 from h04 to h07 and the model's rises +$3.93/+$4.55/+$6.51, 26/21/18 % of it, and the model's whole-day DJF trough-to-peak range is 32/27/21 % of PJM's. Root cause measured: the keeper runs ramp_limits=False, so the LP has NO intertemporal thermal coupling and meets the winter morning ramp with STEAM it ramps 1.8/2.4/2.6x harder than the real fleet instead of the CTs PJM actually starts (model CT rise only 58/76/83 % of actual) -- which also predicts the standing CT_PEAKER -2.11/-3.57/-3.32 TWh C1 note. Successor lever CHARTERED and no-LP PRE-CHECKED: ramp_envelopes (matrix PJM U, CAMPD-measured, ZERO fitted DOF, armed in no keeper in any ISO; p99 1-h up-move model/actual = CC 1.42/1.72/1.53, CT 1.38/1.70/1.52, ST 1.61/1.62/1.50). See PREREG-pjm140-ramp-envelopes-2026-07-30.md and FINDING-pjm139-winter-morning-ramp-is-a-ramp-rate-deficit-2026-07-30.md. Refused until a measured sub-zonal load basis exists. (5) C8 CT_PEAKER forced share rose to 16.3/16.9/17.1 % at pjm-137 (all GROUNDED) on a class whose volume fell 2.6-2.9 TWh -- watch it. (a) THE pjm-122 MARGINAL-OWNERSHIP CHARGE ('fitted coal rungs own the $40-150 region the measured corpus assigns to the CC top belt and CT_FAST') DOES NOT REPRODUCE on the current keeper. The intervening keeper line (the CC_LIKE mid-curve belt, the pjm-135 net-position cut, the pjm-136 zonal loss surface, the pjm-137 measured CT heat rates) is the plausible cause. DO NOT re-run pjm-122's charge as a live diagnosis. (b) THE RESERVE / LP SUPPLY-SIDE TIGHTNESS LANE IS NOT A MISSING MECHANISM. PJM's own published day-ahead market prices synchronized reserve above zero in 84.2/96.7/47.6 % of ALL hours at a cover ratio of 1.00-1.11 and the model's reserve dual is above zero in 0/2/28 hours of 8,760 -- but the requirement is PJM's own measured series (load_pjm_measured_reserve_requirement, validated to 2-4 % against PJM's published DA requirement), the demand curve is PJM's published two-step ORDC (pjm_ordc_curve.csv, M11 4.3.3, $850/$300) and the in-LP per-generator joint-headroom co-optimization that is DESIGNED to price the opportunity cost is armed and is its SOLE owner under rule 19. It clears at $0 because LP reserve supply is 5-10x the requirement -- the LP-vs-MIP boundary pjm-82 named, which the no-MIP mandate makes a DISCLOSURE, not a defect. Lane owner-closed 2026-07-11; requirement-side dynamic reserves adjudicated INERT by measurement. Do NOT propose a reserve/scarcity mechanism for PJM.
